disposition_reason: FDA/CFSAN concise review of Cd mitigation across all foods. Cocoa appears only in (a) the JECFA 2011 statement that mean Cd was 0.1-4.8 mg/kg collectively across crustaceans, organ meats, vegetables, nuts/oilseeds, spices, coffee, tea and cocoa (no cocoa-specific value), and (b) a paragraph noting the Codex Code of Practice for prevention and reduction of Cd in cocoa (in development) and possible Codex MLs for cocoa products. Mitigation measures are generic (soil pH/lime, low-Cd varieties, avoiding phosphate fertilizer, Zn, irrigation-water chloride, removing galvanized/Cd-plated equipment) with no cocoa-specific or numeric outcomes.
disposition_locator: p. 261 (JECFA category range); p. 263 sections 3.1.1-3.1.3; Table 1 p. 265; section 4.2 p. 266

study.material_scope: all foods; cocoa mentioned only at category/codex level

controls.control: Commodity-specific Codex Code of Practice for prevention and reduction of Cd contamination in cocoa (primary production and post-harvest recommendations)
controls.design: code of practice (cited as in development, CAC 2019)
controls.outcome: No numbers; review recommends commodity-specific COPs and notes CCCF considered maximum levels for Cd in cocoa products (citing Abt et al. 2018).

controls.control: Raise soil pH with lime (and biochar, Si fertilizers); select low-Cd varieties; avoid phosphate fertilizers in favour of N and K; add Zn; test irrigation water for chloride
controls.outcome: Generic statements: Cd solubility higher at pH 3.0-5.0, bioavailability reduced above pH 6; no cocoa data or numeric effect sizes.

controls.control: Discontinue cadmium-plated utensils and galvanized equipment in post-harvest/food production

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary does not mention the Codex Code of Practice for Cd in cocoa (section 4.2), the review's only cocoa-specific content.
Stored summary correctly notes the JECFA 0.1-4.8 mg/kg range is collective across categories including cocoa; no cocoa-specific value exists in the primary.
Stored summary lists children's mixed-dish exposure contributors (brownies, chocolate cake); these are out of scope for the cocoa page and give no cocoa concentration.
